strings.name: Karl Deisseroth
strings.summary: Trained in neuroscience, medicine and bioengineering, Deisseroth teaches at Stanford and practices psychiatry. With colleagues he adapted microbial light-sensitive proteins to control neurons, developed optogenetics and advanced CLARITY tissue-clearing imaging, enabling causal studies of circuits and behavior. He shared the 2026 medicine Nobel with Hegemann and Nagel. The research value of these tools does not mean psychiatric disorders have been cured.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced optogenetics and brain-tissue imaging methods, providing tools to study neural circuits, behavior and psychiatric disorders.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Boston, Massachusetts, United States; born in 1971.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Light-controlled neurons
strings.highlights.h1.text: With his team, developed light-sensitive protein methods to regulate neural activity; other teams established the underlying protein discoveries.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Harvard degree (1992); Stanford neuroscience PhD (1998) and MD (2000).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Imaging transparent tissue
strings.highlights.h2.text: His team developed CLARITY, combining hydrogels and tissue processing to preserve structure for three-dimensional imaging.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Shared Nobel Prize
strings.timeline.t1.text: Shared the award with Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Human Neural Circuitry program
strings.timeline.t2.text: With clinical and engineering colleagues, launched an interdisciplinary program studying circuits related to neuropsychiatric disorders.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shared Lasker Award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Shared the basic medical research award with Hegemann and Oesterhelt for light-sensitive protein and optogenetics research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: CLARITY introduced
strings.timeline.t4.text: His team published tissue-clearing methods allowing joint study of structure and molecular components in intact brain tissue.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Optogenetics study published
strings.timeline.t5.text: His team reported using light-sensitive ion channels in neurons to control activity with light pulses.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Established Stanford laboratory
strings.timeline.t6.text: Established his laboratory after psychiatry residency, combining clinical and basic research.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Medical degree
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed his Stanford MD and continued psychiatric training.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Harvard graduation
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed biochemical sciences studies before pursuing medicine and neuroscience at Stanford.
